name: Awl-Crag
description: Awl-Crag is a small, airless rocky world whose surface is dominated by a single monumental peak that rises like a stone awl from the cratered plains. The peak, called the Crag by surveyors, stands twenty-eight kilometers above the surrounding terrain, an impossible height on a world so small that its summit is visible from nearly any point on the surface. The rest of the landscape is a battered wasteland of overlapping impact craters and wind-eroded ridges, the rock scoured to a rough, granular texture by billions of years of solar particle bombardment.

Standing at the base of the Crag, one looks upward along a slope that steepens until it becomes a vertical wall of dark basalt, its face catching the unfiltered starlight and throwing it back in sharp, crystalline reflections from mineral inclusions. The absence of atmosphere means the peak appears razor-sharp against the starfield, its outline unwavering and precise. The silence is total, the temperature extremes brutal, and the low gravity lends every movement a dreamlike quality at odds with the harsh, angular landscape.

Deep scans of the Crag have revealed deposits of exotic matter concentrated near its summit, embedded in the rock in a distribution pattern that does not match any known geological process. The deposits are small but incredibly pure, and their presence at such an altitude on such a small body defies conventional explanations. Some researchers theorize that the Crag itself is not a natural formation but the remnant of something that impacted the planet and lodged in its crust, its exotic matter payload intact.

Awl-Crag's exotic matter deposits make it a target of enormous scientific and economic interest, but the summit location and the lack of atmosphere make extraction extraordinarily challenging. Climbing the Crag in vacuum suits is technically possible but hazardous, and the thermal extremes at the summit create conditions that stress materials to their limits. Several expeditions have reached the summit and returned with samples that confirmed the exotic matter readings, but large-scale extraction remains beyond current capability, leaving the Crag's treasure tantalizingly out of reach.
